status: frozen before any Earth reconstruction result (the map preview output/terrain_erosion_20261107/map_preview_f2.* is uncalibrated and used no Earth data)
question: Does the steady-state erosion generator (scripts/terrain_erosion.py evolve) rebuild real terrain from a hand-map-like sketch (four tiers + the biggest rivers) better than today's tier ramps, in the properties that shape travel and borders?
data: ETOPO 2022 surface elevation at 60 arc-seconds (NOAA NCEI, public domain) via OPeNDAP subsets, on a local equal-area grid of 1.85 km (the map's source pixel is 1.84 km); land = elevation > 0 within the window

sketch.tiers: the true elevation smoothed over 5 km, cut into four classes at the window's quantiles that give the map's tier land shares (70.5 / 12.1 / 10.7 / 6.7 %)
sketch.tops: tier k's top = the cut between k and k+1; tier 4's top = the 95th percentile of tier-4 elevation
sketch.h0: today's construction (rotclimate.geography _tier_ramps + elevation_fullres logic) on the sketch tiers with those tops
sketch.rivers: the true terrain's own routed channels (fastscapelib on the true DEM) with the largest drainage areas, as many channel cells per land cell as the map's marked rivers (27,875 px of the map's land)

candidates: evolve() settings, grid: m in {0.35, 0.45, 0.55}; noise_km in {6, 12, 24}; noise_sigma in {0.2, 0.35, 0.6}; river_boost_km2 in {1000, 3000, 10000}; smooth_px in {0, 0.7}; burn_m 4, rounds 6, lowpass_km 14 fixed. Baseline: h0 itself (today's ramps).

metrics.M1_divides: symmetric mean distance (km) between drainage-divide cells of basins >= 500 km2 routed on the true and on the reconstructed surface
metrics.M2_slopes: Kolmogorov-Smirnov distance between true and reconstructed slope distributions, mean over the four tiers
metrics.M3_new_rivers: F1 within 5 km between reconstructed and true channels >= 500 km2 that are not sketch rivers
metrics.M4_isochrones: mean intersection-over-union of 2-day walking reach (Tobler on slope, 8-neighbour, no land cover) from 30 fixed random land points per window, true against reconstructed
metrics.M5_tier_band: share of each tier's cells within its band +/- 10 % on the true surface (the Earth reference for the map's faithfulness check) and on the reconstruction

selection: C* = the setting with the best mean rank over M1, M2 and M4 across the development windows; M3 and M5 reported

blind_gates.G1: C* beats the ramps baseline on M1 in at least 3 of the 4 blind windows
blind_gates.G2: C* beats the ramps baseline on M2 in at least 3 of 4
blind_gates.G3: C* beats the ramps baseline on M4 in at least 3 of 4
blind_gates.adopt: if G1-G3 pass, C* builds the map's height map v2 (plan B3), whose tier-band check uses the Earth M5 reference minus 5 points instead of a flat 90 %; the owner sees a hillshade preview before anything downstream changes; else the generator is revised and a new blind set declared

amendment_1.status: after the development grid, before any blind window was read or scored
amendment_1.finding: M4 cannot discriminate: on the development windows the 2-day Tobler walking reach on the TRUE terrain overlaps the ramps baseline at IoU 0.915-0.980 and has the same median area (6,321-6,506 vs 6,573-6,657 km2) and circularity (1.144-1.158 vs 1.158-1.168, the 8-neighbour disc). Under this walking model realistic relief does not bend 2-day zones at 1.85 km, so no generator can beat the baseline on M4 (no setting wins in >= 3 of 4 development windows; best mean gain +0.001).
amendment_1.change: G3 (M4) is dropped from the gates and reported only; adoption needs G1 (divides) and G2 (slopes). Recorded consequence for the border question: the disc shape of control is a property of the travel-cost model (Tobler + Soule-Goldman), not of the height map; terrain-channelled travel and land cover need their own Earth test (workstreams A2/C).

blind_result.verdict: Adopted: divides better in 3 of 4 blind windows (Guizhou worse), slope distributions better in 4 of 4; isochrones unchanged (reported). C* builds the map's height map v2 (B3).

map_v2_B3.composition: tier ramps h0 + relief compression x (C* eroded surface - its 14 km lowpass), re-routed sink-free with the marked rivers burned (a 14 km lowpass base spilled across the narrow tier-1 and tier-3 bands even with no detail); development check of this composition: divides 8.4 / 18.7 / 23.4 / 13.6 km and slope KS 0.144 / 0.106 / 0.224 / 0.079 (vs eroded 7.8 / 19.7 / 23.6 / 12.8 and 0.187 / 0.113 / 0.233 / 0.112)
map_v2_B3.climate: the climate keeps today's elevation (climate-grid block means of v2 differ by mean |d| 35 m, p95 179 m, max 911 m in deeply incised mountain blocks); v2 serves travel, rivers, farming and settlement, with a lapse-rate adjustment wherever fine-scale temperature is used
map_v2_B3.status: awaiting owner review of the hillshade preview before anything downstream reads it
